subject: Post-demo: Vector pipeline and migration handoff
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-retail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@acme-retail.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Vector pipeline and migration handoff

Thanks again for the demo earlier — super helpful to see the routing and the reranker flow in action. Quick recap from our side and the questions we promised to surface to make the internal handoff easier:

Summary of what we want to achieve:
- Replace existing embeddings provider for search & recommendations on two services (catalog search, help articles).
- Target latency for k-NN lookup: 15–25ms p95 in our us-west region.
- Transition plan needs zero-downtime indexing and ability to fall back to current provider for the first 2 weeks.

Technical questions / asks (please call these out as concrete items we can track):
1) Vector dimension recommendation: our current vectors are 384-D from VendorX. Is it recommended to keep 384 for parity, or move to 512 for better custo-semantic coverage? Costs + latency impact guidance would be great.
2) Batching defaults: what batch size do you recommend for our steady-state qps (~120 qps across two services) vs. peak (burst to 700 qps)?
3) Normalization and versioning: is Redwood[0m's SDK opinionated about L2 vs. cosine normalization? How should we store versions of vectors in our index during the migration?
4) Auth & routing during migration: we need a minimal auth flow that allows our edge services to call Redwood Dedicated with per-service keys and routing that pins catalog search to GPU-pool-A and help articles to GPU-pool-B. Any sample config or snippet would help accelerate our infra work.

Next steps we suggested internally:
- Organize an ops handoff doc + shared runbook that includes the exact SDK snippets and a migration checklist.
- Pilot: 2-week pilot with 5M vectors (a subset of catalog) + A/B against VendorX.

Attachments: acme-migration-plan.xlsx (high-level timeline), example_export_from_vendorx.csv

Let us know if we missed anything — would like to lock the pilot scope and a short runbook this week so our infra sprint can start next Monday.

Best,
Sarah Jones
Head of Search & Recommendations
ACME Retail

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 18:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Vector pipeline and migration handoff

Thanks Sarah — great notes and thanks for the clear asks. I put a quick-answers section first, then a proposed pilot checklist.

Quick answers:
- Dimension: keep 384 for the initial pilot to maintain parity and simplify A/B. We recommend testing 512 in a controlled eval (quality vs cost) after pilot if you see recall gaps.
- Batching: start with an adaptive batching strategy — target batch sizes ~64 for GPU instances during steady state and allow burst aggregation up to 512 for short windows. Redwood's SDK supports adaptive batch timeouts so you won't have to hard-code aggressive sizes.
- Normalization: Redwood recommends storing raw vectors but normalizing at index time with cosine (unit L2) if you're using cosine similarity; we can also provide a pre-normalized export that matches VendorX. Versioning: add a vector_version tag in metadata and keep the old vectors as version v0 while migrating to v1 so rollbacks are easy.
- Auth & routing snippet: we'll attach a sample redwood-embed-sample-config.yaml with per-service API keys, route definitions, and GPU pool pinning.

Pilot checklist (proposed):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + runbook sign-off (redwood + ACME ops)
2) Week 1: Ingest subset (5M vectors) into a dedicated pool, run A/B traffic split 5/95 (new/old) and smoke tests for p95 latency.
3) Week 2: Increase traffic to 25% for validation, run offline eval comparing recall@10 and reranker F1.
4) Week 3: Full traffic ramp to 100% with fallback route for 2 weeks. Perform SLA burn-in and cost report.

Attachments: redwood-embed-sample-config.yaml (attached), basic migration runbook link: https://drive.redwood/shared/ACME-embed-runbook

Can Marissa and Rishi weigh in on the SLA/price guardrails we should propose for the pilot? I[0m'll also add the SDK snippets to the runbook.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-retail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Vector pipeline and migration handoff

Adding pricing & ops guardrails so ACME can evaluate risk during pilot.

Commercial guardrails for pilot:
- Pilot SKU: reserved pilot capacity with a 4-week credit cap to limit surprise spend. We'll bill on usage but cap the first month to an agreed amount (TBD).
- SLA: we can provide best-effort 99.9% up for Dedicated pools in pilot with a documented fallback to VendorX per your runbook. Formal SLA and long-term discount proposals can be discussed after successful pilot.
- Rollback protection: Redwood supports instant routing overrides; we'll provide a runbook playbook to flip traffic back to VendorX within 5 minutes if latency or correctness regressions are detected.

Operational notes for the infra team:
- SDK samples below (pseudo):
  - python: r = redwood.Client(api_key=\"SERVICE_KEY\"); r.embed.batch_upload(dataset, dim=384, normalize=True, metadata_attr=\"vector_version=v1\")
  - routing: routes:
      - path: /search/catalog
        pool: gpu-pool-A
        auth: service_catalog_key

- Monitoring: recommend adding two alert tiers — latency p95 > 50ms and recall drop > 5% vs baseline. Redwood will push traces to your Datadog project via the shared integration.

I'm attaching a sample config and a short price estimate for the pilot. If ACME agrees, I'll create a pilot order and credit note we can attach to the HubSpot deal record.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot_price_estimate.pdf (stub), redwood-embed-sample-config.yaml
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-retail.com>

Cc: devops@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Vector pipeline and migration handoff

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We reviewed the checklist with our devops and are ready to proceed with the pilot scope as proposed (5M vectors, 2-week A/B ramp, fallback to VendorX). Two small clarifications:

1) Can the adaptive batching be enforced per route? Catalog search needs higher priority and lower latency vs. help articles. We want separate batch timeout knobs per route.
2) For vector_version tagging — can Redwood expose that as a field we can query from our index service so we can show ‘migrated’ vs ‘legacy’ in our admin?

Proposed next actions:
- Monday 9am PT: 30m kick-off with ACME infra + Redwood ops to share the config and exchange keys.
- Marissa: please send the pilot order & credit note so procurement can start the paperwork.

I'll attach the migration spreadsheet with the catalog sample slice. Look forward to the kickoff — we'll circulate the invite now.

Best,
Sarah Jones
Head of Search & Recommendations
ACME Retail
